text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VJESNIK
- NATO leaders expressed their support for Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic.
- More than 2,000 Serb families in Eastern Slavonia want to sell their property and leave, according to the state agency for the sale of real estate in the region.
- Hungary, Poland and Czech Republic to join NATO in the first round.
- Commentary: Figures show a strong rise in the number of visitors on the coast this summer, but not necessarily a larger revenue from tourism.
- The current mandate of a UN observer mission in Prevlaka, the southernmost tip of Croatia, expires on July 15. The Security Council is expected to pass a new resolution on the mandate within days.
- Exports to the European Union rise in the first five months this year but their share of total Croatian exports is shrinking. More goods exported to the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Poland.
VECERNJI LIST

- Croatia is preparing special police forces according to American training programmes to combat drug smuggling. Croatia is near the top of the list of European countries according to the quantity of cocain seized on its territory.
- First Croatian refugees returned to Ilok this week and were put up temporarily until their own houses are vacated by Serb refugees who settled there after fleeing other areas.
- We'll preserve the political centre, says Zlatko Tomcic, president of the peasant party (HSS).
- Hospitals and other state health units short of money: Will patients get small rations of drugs as a result of this situation?
- Supervisory board of the Plomin thermo-electric complex sets the date for the start of works on the second plant Plomin II for September.
- The government has issued guarantees for 2.33 billion kuna worth of loans to companies, mostly shipyards. State firms can count on another 1.7 billion in guarantees this year.
- Kras will remain a Croatian firm, majority owned by small shareholders, says its board president Boris Marcac.
SLOBODNA DALMACIJA
- Croatia demands that the last mandate of the U.N. forces on its territory be ended by January 15, 1998.
- Reshuffle in the foreign ministry: Davorin Rudolf to become a new ambassador to the Vatican, replacing Ivo Livljanic who is retiring.
- The Croatian economy is hostage to the grey economy. Finance Minister Bozo Prka warns it is seriously influencing official policy-making and overall economic trends.
- Austrian airline Tyrolean introduced special flights between June and October to bring tourists to the island of Brac. Hotel Borak in Bol sold out to Austrian for 120 days this summer.

- Private enterprise is the best source of new jobs, says Assistant Economy Minister Vladimir Zanic. For a single dollar invested in small enterprises, the government gets back $12 through tax, better employment and production, Zanic says. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557 075
